claims.sourceText: AFSWC TR-59-39 Vol I, report page and appendix on extraterrestrial-life panels, https://archive.org/download/DTIC_AD0425380/DTIC_AD0425380_djvu.txt
claims.text: The contributor list on the report page includes 'C. E. Sagan' alongside ten others. The report's appendix separately lists 'C. Sagan, U. of Chicago, Astronomy' as a member of the National Academy of Sciences WESTEX group and 'C. Sagan, ARF - Yerkes, Astronomy' on the Armed Forces National Research Council Panel on Extraterrestrial Life. The document says nothing about his security clearance.

claims.nodeLabel: AFSWC TR-59-39 Vol I, A Study of Lunar Research Flights, 19 June 1959
claims.sourceText: AFSWC TR-59-39 Vol I, Chapter I, Introduction, https://archive.org/download/DTIC_AD0425380/DTIC_AD0425380_djvu.txt
claims.text: The introduction states the political motive in the report's own words: 'The motivation for such a detonation is clearly threefold: scientific, military and political... Obviously, however, specific positive effects would accrue to the nation first performing such a feat as a demonstration of advanced technological capability. It is also certain that, unless the climate of world opinion were well-prepared in advance, a considerable negative reaction could be stimulated.'

claims.nodeLabel: AFSWC TR-59-39 Vol I, A Study of Lunar Research Flights, 19 June 1959
claims.sourceText: AFSWC TR-59-39 Vol I, title page and report page, DDC AD 425380, https://archive.org/details/DTIC_AD0425380
claims.text: The report is 'AFSWC-TR-59-39, TR 59-39 Vol I, A STUDY OF LUNAR RESEARCH FLIGHTS', issued by 'HEADQUARTERS AIR FORCE SPECIAL WEAPONS CENTER, AIR RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT COMMAND, KIRTLAND AIR FORCE BASE, NEW MEXICO', authored by L. Reiffel of the Armour Research Foundation, Illinois Institute of Technology, dated 19 June 1959, under Project Number 5776-57853 and Contract AF 29(601)-1164. Its title page marks the title '(Unclassified Title)'. The string 'A119' appears nowhere in the report.

claims.nodeLabel: AFSWC TR-59-39 Vol I, A Study of Lunar Research Flights, 19 June 1959
claims.text: The abstract opens: 'Nuclear detonations in the vicinity of the moon are considered in this report along with scientific information which might be obtained from such explosions. The military aspect is aided by investigation of space environment, detection of nuclear device testing, and capability of weapons in space.'
